pageCache.pageTitle: Mathematics - Curriculum subjects - Madley Brook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
Maths at Madley Brook School
At Madley Brook we have high expectations for every child. Teaching for mastery in Maths is essentially the expectation that all pupils will gain a deep understanding of the maths they are learning. For understanding in Maths to be secure, learning needs to be built on solid foundations.
A mastery approach to the curriculum means pupils spend far longer on fewer key mathematical concepts whilst working at greater depth. Long term gaps in learning are prevented through speedy teacher intervention and those children who grasp the concepts more quickly are given opportunities to deepen their knowledge and improve their reasoning skills rather than accelerating on to new curriculum content.
Problem solving is central and opportunities are given for pupils to calculate with confidence, ensuring an understanding of why it works so that pupils understand what they are doing rather than just learning to repeat routines without grasping what is happening.
Children will be learning in a practical, visual and written way. All children across the school will be given access to practical equipment and encouraged to use it to deepen their understanding.

pageCache.pageTitle: Phonics - Curriculum subjects - Madley Brook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Phonics
Read, Write, Inc. Phonics
At Madley Brook School, phonics is taught using the Read Write Inc. scheme, which ensures systematic coverage and progression. Children begin formal phonics lessons in their Reception year. Phonics is taught in small groups focusing on children's recognition of the letter sounds and how to read and write these. They take home and practise reading a copy of the same book, which they are also reading in class. Reading this book, at home regularly with an adult, supports their reading progress in school.
In Reception and Key Stage 1 children are taught in smaller groups, led either by the class teacher or by trained learning support staff. The children are assessed regularly to ensure that they are in the appropriate group for supporting and extending their individual needs. Year 1 children take part in statutory Phonics Screening during the summer term, and parents are informed of their child's achievement at the end of the school year.

Breakfast Club is ran by Ms Ng and Mrs Powell Monday-Friday (term time only) from 7:30-8:30am
Each session costs £5 per child, per day and payments must be made in advance.
Bookings and payments are to be made using your MCAS account. If you need support with this then please contact the school office
